constructed: the four words the build session gave each reference release from the text releases --reference wrote through the anonymiser at 175a444d0383, under the instruction's own words and before the local model read any of them; the anonymiser at fe22a6282817 writes the same texts again differing only by a code page's characters and neutral words
questions: results, "how the release describes the quarter against what was expected": better where the release itself says the quarter beat what was expected, its own guidance, outlook or the consensus (exceeded, above the high end, ahead of, better than expected, surpassed); in line where it says the quarter met them (in line with, within the range, as expected, met); worse where it says the quarter fell short (below, missed, short of, lower than expected); not stated where it compares the quarter with no expectation, however good or bad its figures read against the year before. Records and growth alone are not a comparison with what was expected.

outlook, "what the release does to the outlook": raised where any guided figure for a period is raised from what was guided before; lowered or withdrawn where any is lowered, withdrawn or suspended (lowered wins where a release raises one figure and lowers another); kept where it reaffirms, maintains or reiterates, or issues guidance for a period with no earlier guidance compared; none given where it states no forward figure or range at all.

tone, "the tone of management's own words": the quoted words of its officers alone. confident where they speak of strength, momentum, records, confidence or being well positioned with no caution weighing against it; cautious where they name headwinds, uncertainty, challenges, softness or disappointment as what the quarter or the year turns on; neutral where they report without either, or balance the two evenly. No quote, neutral.

demand, "how the release describes demand or orders": stronger where it says demand, orders, bookings, backlog, traffic or volumes grew or were strong; weaker where it says they fell, softened or saw destocking or cancellations; steady where it says they held stable; not stated where it says nothing about demand or orders. Revenue growth alone is not demand.
conventions: results: a central measure of the quarter said to be better than expected (credit quality for a bank) is better; a multi-year programme's target beaten is not the quarter against what was expected, so not stated.
outlook: guidance a release gives by direction alone for a coming period ("significantly lower than the quarter") is guidance issued, so kept, unless it raises or cuts what was guided before.
tone: headwinds named as overcome, beside strength and confidence, is confident; strength and caution weighed evenly (records beside softening markets and contingency plans) is neutral.
demand: where a release describes demand both strengthening and softening in about equal measure (backlog up, some regions soft), steady.
outlook: guidance a release gives with no earlier guidance set beside it is kept, whatever an earlier release said, since the labels come from the text alone.

outlook: any forward financial figure for the business, capital spending or a one-time cost estimate among them, is a guided figure, so a release stating one is never none given; none given is kept for a release with no forward figure or range at all.
results: "at the high end of" guidance is within it, so in line; "above the high end" is better.

outlook: raised or lowered is read off the headline figures, sales, earnings or EPS, operating income or EBITDA, FFO, production and cash flow; a component, a margin, a cost line, the tax rate, capital spending or the share count, decides only where no headline figure moved. Lowered wins where one headline figure rises and another falls.
outlook: a standing policy target with no period, a leverage range the release itself says is not guidance, is not a guided figure, so a release stating nothing else forward is none given.
outlook: a coming quarter's headline figures lowered beside the full year's raised is lowered or withdrawn, since lowered wins whatever the periods the figures cover.
demand: a bank's loans grown, or a lender's originations, are its volumes, so stronger; loan demand said to be soft or loans shrinking for want of demand is weaker.
results: a release saying the quarter as a whole was as expected is in line, though it names one line, as the margin, as better or worse than expected.

outlook: a sum the company is bound to pay, as deferred pay, and a view of the market's course with no figure or direction for the company's own results are not guidance, so none given where nothing else is stated.
results: management saying it was not satisfied with or disappointed by the quarter, naming no expectation, guidance or consensus it fell short of, is not stated; the tone question takes it.
demand: a retailer's comparable or same-store sales are revenue, so they decide demand only with traffic, transactions, units or volumes named beside them; comparable sales alone are not stated.
outlook: an officer's remark that a trend should go on (the margin should keep expanding), with no period and no figure, is not guidance, so none given where nothing else is stated.
results: where the release says one headline figure beat what was expected and another fell short (earnings above guidance, sales below its low end), worse, as lowered wins for the outlook.
outlook: a long-term target the release says it will now reach earlier than it anticipated is raised, the release itself setting the new outlook against the old.
results: a release whose own heading says the quarter exceeded expectations is better, though one line inside it is at the high end of guidance, none falling short.

outlook: guidance the release says it updates because of uncertainty or a weakening market, the earlier figures not stated, is lowered or withdrawn; an update the release says follows strength is raised; an update naming no cause and no earlier figure is kept.
demand: a bank's loans falling because loans are repaid or forgiven, the release naming no want of demand, is not stated.
demand: a table of occupancy or volumes that no sentence describes is not stated; the release's words decide.
outlook: a range narrowed about the same midpoint is kept for that figure; another headline figure raised makes the release raised.
outlook: a range reiterated with results now expected in its upper half, beside another guided figure raised and none cut, is raised.

outlook: a sum the company expects to receive under what it holds (its securities' principal running off) is not guidance, as a sum it is bound to pay is not; a bank saying it is encouraged by the near-term outlook, with no figure, is not guidance either.
demand: demand said to remain healthy or strong is stronger, the level said being strong; steady is for demand said to hold flat, stable or unchanged.
demand: volumes up for the whole company (with acquisitions) and down for the same stores, both stated, are mixed, so steady.
results: an operating count beating the company's own expectations (communities open) is not the quarter's results against what was expected, so not stated where nothing else is compared.
results: a bank saying its asset quality performed within its expectations, nothing else compared, is in line, as credit quality better than expected is better.
demand: a bank naming lower lending activity is weaker, though its average loans held about flat.
outlook: an operating milestone brought forward (a plant back in service earlier than scheduled) is not a guided figure; the financial guidance decides.
demand: transactions (traffic) down overall is weaker, though they are said to be improving or rise in one region.
outlook: an officer's qualitative hope for a period (strong free cash flow this year), with no figure and no direction against a base, is not guidance, so none given where nothing else is stated.
outlook: a release saying it is on track for the financial objectives it set earlier reiterates them, so kept.
demand: an insurer's premiums written moving on reinsurance changes or a business sold, no demand described, is not stated.

outlook: the GAAP and adjusted versions of one figure moving apart are one figure; a GAAP figure the release only revises for a charge already taken, beside the adjusted figure and cash flow raised, is raised. Lowered still wins between different headline figures or periods.
demand: one segment's volumes up, another's flat and a third's down by a planned exit is mixed, so steady.
outlook: a range replaced by a point inside it is moved by its midpoint (revenue to near the old low end is lowered), and lowered still wins over another headline figure raised.
demand: bookings said to decline year over year are weaker, though the chief executive calls them improved.
results: results said to "reflect the expected impact" of an item are not the quarter set against what was expected, so not stated.
demand: an insurer's new business said to be higher and premium growth said to accelerate is stronger, though policies in force held flat.
outlook: a cash runway stated as the year the company is funded into, and payments a partner is bound to make, are not guided figures, so none given where nothing else is stated.
demand: a net lease REIT's investment volume and deal pipeline are its volumes, as a lender's originations are, so a record volume and an active pipeline are stronger.
results: one segment said to grow "as expected" is not the quarter set against what was expected, so not stated where nothing else is compared.
results: a producer saying its volumes run higher than expected, the central measure of its quarter, is better.
demand: demand for the company's product said to be expected to grow is stronger.
demand: an asset gatherer's net inflows in some businesses beside net outflows in another are mixed, so steady.
demand: leases signed and leasing spreads reported with no comparison of volumes and no word on demand are not stated.
outlook: an officer expecting further growth and margin expansion in the coming fiscal year gives a direction against the year just ended for a named period, so kept, unlike a hope with no base.
demand: a miner's own production (blocks won, hashrate) is output, not demand for what it sells, so not stated where no customer demand is described.

demand: a utility's customers added (connections, meters) said to grow strongly are its volumes, as a bank's loans are, so stronger; capacity committed to customers under long contracts is demand too.
results: one headline figure said to be in line with expectations and another ahead of them, none short, is better, as one guided figure kept beside another raised is raised.
results: one segment's revenue said to be lower than expected, offset by the others and the quarter as a whole set against no expectation, is not stated, as one segment growing as expected is.
demand: one business's demand said to weaken while another's volumes grow, the release setting the one against the other as offsetting, is mixed, so steady.

demand: volumes named only as a cause of a margin's move, in parts of one segment ("higher costs and lower volumes in parts of the segment"), are not the release describing demand, so not stated where nothing else is said.
outlook: the part of the backlog expected to become revenue within twelve months is a contracted sum's timing, not guidance, so none given where nothing else forward is stated.

results: a quarter said to come in strong against expectations, its figures named as near the high end of guidance and above its midpoint, is within the range, so in line; "strong against" is none of the words that beat it.
